messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - continuous-batching performance cliff detected on rwd-prod-eu-1. Symptoms: sustained 95th latency spike (>3s), microbatch inflight queue growth, KV cache eviction rate has spiked. Affected service: hosted /v1/generate routes. Alert id=alb-0xabc123. Paging eng-oncall. :rotating_light:

alex: i'm taking this. seeing queue length jump and a lot of microbatches sitting in the queue. can someone pull recent rollout diffs?

maria: rollout from last night bumped continuous_batch.microbatch_target -> 8 (intended to improve throughput). kvcache size doubled on some instances; eviction storms visible. looks like thrashing: large batches evict hot prefixes, then cache misses increase latency.

alex: ok probable root: microbatch target too large under high concurrency + no jitter -> synchronized batches + cache churn. mitigation plan: reduce microbatch_target, add batching jitter, tune kvcache eviction factor, and limit concurrent inflight per worker.

ryan: +1. also consider applying a soft cap to auto-scaling of microbatch_target in config so it can't jump to 8 under sudden QPS spikes.

alex: going to patch cluster config to a small canary: microbatch_target=2, batch_jitter_ms=40, kvcache.eviction_factor=0.6, concurrent_inflight_per_worker=256. rolling canary 5% first. command i'm about to run:
```bash
redwoodctl rollout config set --cluster rwd-prod-eu-1 \
  --path continuous_batch.microbatch_target=2 \
  --path continuous_batch.batch_jitter_ms=40 \
  --path kvcache.eviction_factor=0.6 \
  --path scheduler.concurrent_inflight_per_worker=256 \
  --canary 5
```

ops-bot: Started rollout canary 5% for config change (rollout id rup-20260315-77). Monitor dashboards: https://internal.ops/rollouts/rup-20260315-77

maria: early signal looks promising on canary hosts: queue depth flattening, p95 down ~18% on nodes with new config. evictions on those hosts down ~60%.

alex: increasing canary to 25%.

ops-bot: Canary updated -> 25%.

eva: FYI support metrics: a small spike in 429s (~0.8%) correlated with the cliff window, mostly from high-concurrency API keys. Not seeing data loss. I've alerted CS to proactively notify top customers if needed.

alex: temporary customer-facing mitigation: enable fallback routing for known high-QPS API keys to disable continuous batching for them until cold caches warm. started a small routing change for profile_x keys.

ryan: command to patch route fallback (applied):
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","fallback_mode":"disable_continuous_batching","target_profile":"profile_x"}
```

maria: important: after config change we'll need to prime the KV cache for hot prefixes (warmup). plan: run synthetic requests for top-200 prefixes across affected regions.

alex: copying runbook checklist: monitor: p95/p99 latency, queue depth, kvcache hitrate, eviction rate, 429 rate. I want someone watching logs for "microbatch_wait_timeout" and "kv_evict_rate_high" alerts.

eva: i'm on customer watch and will update tickets. notified 3 impacted accounts; they reported degraded latency but not timeouts.

(rolling canary observation window ~7m)

maria: metrics stable for 7m; 25% hosts show sustained improvement. no regressions so far on throughput.

alex: proceeding to 100% rollout now.

ops-bot: Rollout rup-20260315-77 progressing -> 100% completed.

maria: post-hotfix summary metrics: microbatch_target 8 -> 2, batch_jitter_ms 0 -> 40ms, kvcache.eviction_factor 1.0 -> 0.6, concurrent_inflight_per_worker capped -> 256. p95 latency improved ~33% cluster-wide, kvcache evictions down ~70%, 429 rate returned to baseline (~0.09%).

ryan: handoff notes for night oncall: incident mitigated but follow-ups required:
- run load replay for 5 patterns at 5k concurrent QPS to validate no regressions
- add guardrail to prevent microbatch_target auto-increment > 4 during abrupt load spikes
- add a metric alert for microbatch_target increases and kvcache eviction rate > threshold
- create a synthetic warmup job to run after future batch-related rollouts

alex: i'll file the postmortem (include blast radius, timeline, metrics graphs, and the config delta). also proposing a quick unit test in the scheduler to simulate jitter effect under high concurrency.

eva: i've flagged affected customers in CS and included mitigation notes. no escalations open.

ryan: i'll take the remainder of the oncall for the night and keep monitoring. marking this thread as 'mitigated' for active measures; postmortem still pending.

alex: thanks all. great coordination. please add any missed action items to the postmortem doc.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied, severity lowered to P2, automatic paging suppressed for 2 hours. Incident record: ir-20260315-77. :white_check_mark:
